svg.title: Promptly (Windows desktop)
svg.desc: System-tray dictation app for Windows: a user-chosen global hotkey records the microphone, Groq Whisper transcribes (or translates), a fast Groq AI model polishes the text using the user's personal vocabulary, and the result is pasted or copied. Ships as a single PyInstaller exe with single-instance guarding, two overlay designs, automatic retry of connection failures, an amber paused state that keeps the recording in RAM, and launch-with-Windows support.

main.py entry point
g.desc: Redirects stderr to promptly-crash.log in windowed builds, creates the QApplication, enforces the single-instance lock, then constructs PromptlyApp and enters the Qt event loop.. Purpose: Process entry point for dev runs and the packaged exe.. How it works: _redirect_crash_log captures stderr next to the exe and keeps print() safe when PyInstaller provides no stdout. main() then sets high-DPI pass-through, builds the QApplication with QuitOnLastWindowClosed disabled, acquires the SingleInstance lock (a second launch exits 0 after notifying the first), wires the activation callback to PromptlyApp.activate_existing_instance, and runs the app.. Inputs: process start. Outputs: Qt event loop running. Dependencies: PromptlyApp orchestrator; SingleInstance guard. Evidence: main.py: _redirect_crash_log; main.py: main(); main.py: single_instance.acquire(). Chart: Source lines per module. Independent categories; bars are not connected. overlay.py: 1098 lines; app.py: 1096 lines; settings_dialog.py: 314 lines; hotkey.py: 175 lines; transcriber.py: 160 lines; single_instance.py: 123 lines; recorder.py: 121 lines; polisher.py: 117 lines; startup.py: 94 lines; paster.py: 88 lines; main.py: 71 lines. Unit: lines. Evidence: wc -l line counts measured from repository source files, 2026-10-08. Source: main.py

g.title: SingleInstance guard
g.desc: One Promptly process at a time: a named Windows mutex decides ownership, and a QLocalServer/QLocalSocket channel lets later launches ask the running instance to show itself.. Purpose: Prevent duplicate tray apps and hotkey conflicts.. How it works: acquire() uses kernel32 CreateMutexW on Local\Promptly.SingleInstance; ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS means another instance owns the app, so the newcomer connects a QLocalSocket, writes 'activate', and exits. The owner listens on the same name and invokes the activation callback (show the overlay). Non-Windows dev environments fall back to the local server alone.. Inputs: second process launch. Outputs: activation callback on the running instance. Dependencies: PromptlyApp orchestrator. Evidence: single_instance.py: MUTEX_NAME; single_instance.py: _acquire_windows_mutex; single_instance.py: _notify_existing_instance. Source: single_instance.py

g.title: PromptlyApp
g.desc: Main orchestrator: owns tray, overlay, recorder, hotkey and workers; runs the IDLE / RECORDING / TRANSCRIBING / DONE / ERROR / PAUSED state machine, caches the recording in RAM while transcription is pending, and applies every setting live.. Purpose: Wire all components into one voice-to-text flow with resilient delivery.. How it works: Toggle (hotkey, overlay, tray) starts/stops recording. On stop, audio is WAV-encoded in memory (never on disk) and handed to a TranscriptionWorker with model/language/mode/polish/vocab from settings. A retryable failure that survives 3 attempts enters PAUSED: the amber overlay keeps the cached bytes until the user retries (retry_requested) or discards (closing the overlay while paused). Success pastes or copies per the auto_paste setting, with clipboard fallback. Launch syncs the startup entry and registers the saved hotkey, which can be replaced transactionally after Settings saves.. Inputs: hotkey press; overlay toggle/close/retry signals; tray menu actions; worker done/error/retry/polish signals. Outputs: recorder start/stop; worker start; paste/copy request; tray icon, tooltip and balloon updates; startup sync. Dependencies: TranscriptionWorker; AudioRecorder; Overlay windows; Global hotkey; Auto-paster; Settings dialog; Startup manager; QSettings store. Evidence: app.py: PromptlyApp._toggle; app.py: _stop_and_transcribe; app.py: _enter_paused; app.py: _retry_pending; app.py: _on_transcription_done; app.py: _replace_hotkey. Source: app.py

g.title: TranscriptionWorker
g.desc: Background QThread that resets the Groq client, transcribes or translates, automatically retries transient connection failures (3 attempts, 2 s / 4 s delays), then optionally polishes the transcript before emitting done.. Purpose: Keep the UI responsive and make brief network blips self-heal.. How it works: run() sets transcriber._client to None so the API key is re-read, then loops up to MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 calling transcribe() or translate_to_english(). Exceptions classified by is_retryable_error schedule the next attempt (retry_scheduled signal) with cancellable sleeps. After a transcript arrives, polish_started fires and polish_text() runs; any polish failure falls back to the raw Whisper text. error(message, retryable) only fires when cancelled is false.. Inputs: WAV bytes or file path; model, language, mode; polish flag; vocab list. Outputs: done(text); error(message, retryable); retry_scheduled(attempt, max); polish_started. Dependencies: Groq transcriber; AI polisher. Evidence: app.py: TranscriptionWorker.run; app.py: MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3; app.py: RETRY_DELAYS = (2.0, 4.0). Source: app.py

g.title: AudioRecorder
g.desc: Records the default microphone via sounddevice at 16 kHz mono, maintains a smoothed level for the live volume meter, and WAV-encodes recordings entirely in memory.. Purpose: Capture microphone audio without touching the disk.. How it works: start() opens a sounddevice InputStream (float32) and appends chunks; each callback also updates level = 0.5*level + 0.5*min(1, (rms*25)^0.75). stop() closes the stream and returns the concatenated array. wav_bytes() encodes to BytesIO WAV and returns None under the 0.5 s MIN_DURATION. Failures during start() re-raise after cleanup so the app can show its mic error.. Inputs: microphone stream callback chunks. Outputs: numpy audio array; in-memory WAV bytes; level (0..1). Dependencies: Microphone (default input device). Evidence: recorder.py: AudioRecorder.start; recorder.py: wav_bytes; recorder.py: level property. Source: recorder.py

g.title: Microphone (default input device)
g.desc: The system's default recording device, opened by sounddevice at 16 kHz mono.. Purpose: Source of raw audio.. How it works: Accessed only through recorder.py; a missing device raises into PromptlyApp._start_recording, which shows the no-mic error overlay.. Outputs: 16 kHz mono float32 audio frames. Evidence: recorder.py: sd.InputStream(...); app.py: No microphone found message

g.title: Groq transcriber
g.desc: Groq client singleton plus the speech calls: transcribe() (with language and vocabulary spelling hint) and translate_to_english(); also classifies which errors are worth retrying.. Purpose: Turn recordings into text using Groq's Whisper models.. How it works: The API key comes from QSettings('Promptly','Promptly') api_key, sanitized to its first whitespace token. transcribe() accepts a path or WAV bytes (bytes are wrapped as audio.wav in a BytesIO so nothing hits disk) and adds language and prompt=vocab_prompt(vocab) when present. translate_to_english() uses the audio.translations endpoint and only whisper-large-v3 supports it. is_retryable_error() treats HTTP 429/5xx, connection/timeout types and message markers as transient; auth-type errors fail fast.. Inputs: audio path or WAV bytes; model, language; vocab list. Outputs: transcribed/translated text; retryable classification. Dependencies: Groq Whisper API; QSettings store. Evidence: transcriber.py: _get_api_key; transcriber.py: transcribe; transcriber.py: translate_to_english; transcriber.py: is_retryable_error. Source: transcriber.py

g.title: AI polisher
g.desc: Cleans the raw transcript with Groq chat model openai/gpt-oss-20b (temperature 0, reasoning_effort low): grammar, fillers, broken sentences — meaning and language untouched. Teaches the user's word list and falls back to the raw text on refusal or empty output.. Purpose: Make dictated speech read like clean typing.. How it works: polish() wraps the transcript in <transcript> tags as data, sends the strict cleanup system prompt plus _vocab_block(vocab) (a phrase sounding like a listed term is rewritten to its exact spelling; genuine similar-sounding words stay), and returns the model text. _looks_like_refusal compares _REFUSAL_MARKERS against polished vs original, so refusals the user never spoke return the original transcript instead.. Inputs: raw transcript; vocab list. Outputs: polished text or the original. Dependencies: Groq chat API; Groq transcriber. Evidence: polisher.py: polish; polisher.py: _SYSTEM_PROMPT; polisher.py: _vocab_block; polisher.py: _looks_like_refusal. Source: polisher.py

g.title: Global hotkey
g.desc: parse_hotkey() converts the user's QKeySequence string to a Windows virtual key plus modifiers (a bare key is rejected); GlobalHotkey registers it with RegisterHotKey and polls WM_HOTKEY on a daemon thread, reporting failure through on_fail.. Purpose: Start/stop dictation from anywhere with the user's chosen combination.. How it works: register() starts a listener thread, signals readiness via a threading.Event and returns whether Windows accepted the key. The callback fires on that background thread; the app bridges with pyqtSignal. Failed registration (combination held by another app) triggers the tray warning path.. Inputs: WM_HOTKEY message. Outputs: registered callback (background thread); on_fail callback. Dependencies: Windows user32 hotkey API. Evidence: hotkey.py: parse_hotkey; hotkey.py: GlobalHotkey.register; app.py: _replace_hotkey. Source: hotkey.py

g.title: Auto-paster
g.desc: Delivers the transcript: verifies the clipboard copy with pyperclip, then injects Ctrl+V via Win32 SendInput; raises RuntimeError when Windows rejects the input so the app can fall back to copy-only.. Purpose: Put the finished text where the user is typing.. How it works: copy_to_clipboard() copies, sleeps 50 ms and re-pastes to verify. paste_into_terminal() then sends Control down, V down, V up, Control up through SendInput, checking each call's return value.. Inputs: final text. Outputs: clipboard content; simulated Ctrl+V keystrokes. Dependencies: Windows clipboard and keyboard. Evidence: paster.py: copy_to_clipboard; paster.py: paste_into_terminal; app.py: paste fallback to copy_to_clipboard. Source: paster.py

g.title: Windows clipboard and keyboard
g.desc: OS clipboard (pyperclip) and the user32 SendInput keyboard device used to inject Ctrl+V into whatever window has focus.. Purpose: OS-level delivery channel for the transcript.. How it works: pyperclip copy/verify plus the ctypes _INPUT structures in paster.py.. Inputs: text to copy; key events. Outputs: pasted text in the active window. Evidence: paster.py: user32.SendInput; paster.py: pyperclip.copy

g.title: Startup manager
g.desc: Launch-with-Windows support: enables, disables or refreshes the 'Promptly' value under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run. Only the frozen exe ever registers; dev runs are refused at this layer.. Purpose: Bring the tray app and its hotkeys back after every reboot, and self-heal a moved exe because the entry is rewritten at every launch.. How it works: is_enabled() checks the value; enable() writes the quoted exe path (REG_SZ) via winreg; disable() deletes it (already-gone counts as success); sync(enabled) is called at every app launch and again immediately when Settings saves the auto_start checkbox.. Inputs: auto_start preference; launch of the app. Outputs: Run-key value created, refreshed or deleted. Dependencies: Windows startup Run key. Evidence: startup.py: RUN_KEY_PATH; startup.py: enable / disable / sync; app.py: sync_startup(bool(settings.value('auto_start', True, type=bool))). Uncertainty: Real reboot behavior was pending owner confirmation at ship time (per workspace notes); the code path itself is complete.. Source: startup.py

g.title: Windows startup Run key
g.desc: The registry list Windows reads at sign-in: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, value name 'Promptly', pointing at the exe.. Purpose: OS startup list entry.. How it works: Managed exclusively by startup.py through winreg under HKEY_CURRENT_USER.. Inputs: enable/disable/sync calls. Outputs: app launched at sign-in by Windows. Evidence: startup.py: winreg.OpenKey(winreg.HKEY_CURRENT_USER, RUN_KEY_PATH)

g.title: Overlay windows (Classic + Minimal)
g.desc: Two swappable always-on-top designs sharing one interface: the 340x44 Game-Bar-style bar (Overlay) with equalizer meter and timer, and the 116x29 monochrome pill (MinimalOverlay) with painted waveform, orbiting retry arc, and tap/hold hit-testing. Both expose ready / recording / transcribing / done / error / paused / retrying states.. Purpose: Visual feedback and touch/click control for the whole flow.. How it works: State methods restyle the window; update_recording(elapsed, level) refreshes timer and meter ~20x/sec; set_busy_note shows 'Retrying 2/3' or 'Polishing…'. The paused state swaps the action button for a Retry button and emits retry_requested; toggle_requested and close_requested cover the rest. Switching styles in Settings preserves screen position (app.py _set_overlay_style).. Inputs: state calls from PromptlyApp; mouse drag / taps. Outputs: toggle_requested / close_requested / retry_requested signals. Dependencies: PromptlyApp orchestrator. Evidence: overlay.py: Overlay; overlay.py: MinimalOverlay; overlay.py: retry_requested = pyqtSignal(); app.py: _create_overlay. Source: overlay.py

g.aria-label: System tray icon and menu, Frontend
g.title: System tray icon and menu
g.desc: App-icon SVG with a state-colored badge dot (gray/red/blue/green/amber; drawn mic fallback), context menu (overlay, test with file, settings, quit), left-click overlay toggle, and balloon warnings for errors and hotkey conflicts.. Purpose: Persistent control surface and notifier while the app lives in the tray.. How it works: _create_icon renders app-icon.svg via QSvgRenderer (bundled next to the exe through PyInstaller _MEIPASS) and overlays the badge; _setup_tray wires the menu; balloons carry the amber 'recording saved' guidance and hotkey-failure warnings.. Inputs: state changes; user clicks. Outputs: menu actions; balloon notifications. Dependencies: PromptlyApp orchestrator. Evidence: app.py: _create_icon; app.py: _setup_tray; app.py: _on_hotkey_failed. Source: app.py

g.title: Settings dialog
g.desc: Modal dialog storing eleven keys in QSettings: api_key, model, mode (transcribe/translate), language (17 options), auto_paste, polish_text, custom_vocab, overlay_style, overlay_auto_hide, auto_start, hotkey. Saves apply the startup entry immediately; the hotkey is validated with parse_hotkey before saving.. Purpose: One place to configure every behavior of the app.. How it works: Translate mode locks the model to whisper-large-v3 and disables the language picker. The vocab box stores one term per line, trimmed, as custom_vocab. On save, sync_startup(auto_start) runs right away; app.py then swaps the hotkey and overlay style/visibility without a restart.. Inputs: user input: key, model, mode, language, checkboxes, vocab, overlay style, hotkey. Outputs: QSettings writes; startup sync call. Dependencies: QSettings store; Startup manager; Global hotkey. Evidence: settings_dialog.py: _save_settings; settings_dialog.py: _on_mode_changed; settings_dialog.py: sync_startup(auto_start). Source: settings_dialog.py

g.title: QSettings store
g.desc: Persistent settings under 'Promptly'/'Promptly' (Windows registry on this platform). Holds api_key, model, mode, language, auto_paste, polish_text, custom_vocab, overlay_style, overlay_auto_hide, auto_start and hotkey.. Purpose: Single durable configuration store — the app deliberately keeps no .env file.. How it works: Read by PromptlyApp (hotkey, model, language, mode, polish, vocab, auto_paste, overlay settings, auto_start), by the Settings dialog, and by transcriber._get_api_key.. Inputs: settings writes from the dialog and hotkey replacement. Outputs: configuration values to every reader. Evidence: app.py: QSettings('Promptly', 'Promptly') in _check_first_launch, _get_model, _get_vocab; settings_dialog.py: self._settings = QSettings('Promptly', 'Promptly'); transcriber.py: _get_api_key

g.title: Groq Whisper API
g.desc: Groq's cloud speech service: audio/transcriptions (whisper-large-v3-turbo or whisper-large-v3, optional language and vocabulary prompt) and audio/translations (whisper-large-v3 only) for translate mode.. Purpose: Cloud transcription and translation backend.. How it works: Reached through the Groq SDK with response_format text; uploads arrive as a path or as in-memory WAV bytes with filename audio.wav.. Inputs: audio upload; model, language, prompt; Groq API key. Outputs: transcript text / English translation. Evidence: transcriber.py: client.audio.transcriptions.create; transcriber.py: client.audio.translations.create. Uncertainty: Server-side model availability and latency are not observable from this repository.

g.title: Groq chat API
g.desc: Groq's chat/completions endpoint running openai/gpt-oss-20b for transcript cleanup, called with temperature 0 and reasoning_effort low for deterministic, fast results.. Purpose: Grammar/filler cleanup and vocabulary-correct spelling.. How it works: One call per recording with the cleanup system prompt (plus vocab lessons) and the transcript wrapped in <transcript> tags.. Inputs: system + user messages; Groq API key. Outputs: polished text. Evidence: polisher.py: client.chat.completions.create; polisher.py: _MODEL = 'openai/gpt-oss-20b'
